title: R’ Chagga of Tzippori

paragraphs: [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1181&lang=en) cites Shekalim, chapter 1, but Hyman says he has not found it there. In Hyman’s reading of [Shekalim 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.1.1.9), Rabbi Huna Rabbah of Tzippori reports a custom instituted there by Rabbi Chanina.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Guggenheimer digital text of Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 1:1 fully writes Rabbi Chuna Rabbah of Tzippori, supporting Rabbi Huna for ר״ה in this occurrence. Hyman’s nonmatch for Chagga is his observation, not a new exhaustive finding.

The supplied heading’s ר׳ is retained as R’ because the cited Jerusalem Talmud passage names Rabbi Chuna, rather than Chagga. Hyman’s report of Seder HaDorot and his failure to find Chagga remain attributed observations; no identification of the two names is asserted.

[Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1181&lang=en) names Chaga and gives only the chapter. The corresponding statement in [Shekalim 1:1:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shekalim.1.1.9) names Chuna Rabbah and presents the ruling as a local custom.
